title: A p-value is not the odds you are right

probes.question: Which does a p-value actually describe?
options: The chance your hypothesis is true
How unlikely such an extreme result would be if the null hypothesis were true
The chance the result was a fluke

probes.question: True or false: a p-value measures the importance of a result.

image.alt: A histogram of random data forming a bell-shaped Gaussian curve with a smooth curve overlaid.

body.claim: A p-value is not the probability that your hypothesis is true, or that your result was a fluke.
body.why: A p-value says how unlikely a result this extreme would be if the null hypothesis were true. In 2016 the American Statistical Association stated that p-values do not measure the probability that the studied hypothesis is true or that the data were produced by chance alone, nor the size or importance of an effect.
